title: definition payload
description: What a paper takes a term to mean. Carries no numeric value and no adopt/reject stance, so DEFINITION_CONFLICT is the only detector that can see a disagreement here: two papers measuring the same named quantity under incompatible criteria compute different numbers and never know it.

term.description: Normalized name of the term being defined, e.g. attack_success or task_failure. Two papers align on this, not on the definition text - named after the definition, two papers that genuinely disagree about what a word means would land in different clusters and never be compared.

definition.description: The term's meaning as the paper states it, in the paper's own words.

criterion.description: The operational test the definition reduces to - the thing code would actually check. 'the agent executes any action outside the granted capability set' is a criterion; 'a security violation' is not. This is the field DEFINITION_CONFLICT compares, because two definitions that read differently but reduce to the same check are not in conflict, and two that read similarly but reduce to different checks are.

attribution.description: Whether this is the paper's own definition or a restatement of another work's. A related-work section quoting a predecessor's definition is not this paper adopting it.
